text.p: Grain and oilseed exports reported by USDA and private export sources.

SOYBEAN SALE - The Taichung division of Taiwan's Breakfast Soybean Procurement Association bought two 54,000-tonne shipments of U.S. soybeans at a tender on Tuesday. Both shipments were bought from Continental on a cost-and-freight basis. One shipment was set for Dec 20-Jan 3, U.S. Gulf and/or Jan 4-19, PNW at 87.90 US cents/Jan. Another shipment was for Jan 16-30, U.S. Gulf and/or Feb 1-15, PNW, at 84.90 cents/Jan.

VEGOIL SALE - Morocco bought 49,500 tonnes optional origin vegetable oil -- soybean oil or rapeseed oil at seller's option -- for November/December arrival, U.S. exporters said. The oil was acquired at $532.50 a tonne, FOB.
WHEAT TENDER - Slovenia was expected to tender early next week for 35,000 to 40,000 tonnes U.S. hard red spring wheat, U.S. exporters said. Shipment was slated for October 12-November 15.
- The Taiwan Flour Mills Association is expected to place a tender within two weeks for two 34,000-tonne shipments of U.S. wheat, local traders said. No details were available.
WHEAT TENDER - Moroccan millers' group Comite Professionnel de la Minoterie is tendering for 18,500 tonnes optional soft wheat for delivery in the second half October.
- Sri Lanka October 18 seeks 100,000 tonnes optional-origin wheat. It said 50,000 tonnes would be soft white wheat and 50,000 tonnes hard red winter wheat for November 11-20 shipment.
- Syria's General Establishment for Cereal Processing and Trade offered 100,000 tonnes of hard amber durum wheat for November. Oct 1 was the final date for offers. Confirmation is set on October 2.
CORN TENDER - Moroccan feedstuffs group Association des Fabricants d'Aliments Composes is to tender for 20,000 tonnes of maize, probably next week, a spokesman said. No delivery dates have been set.

CORN AND SOYBEAN TENDERS - Taiwanese buyers are expected to hold four tenders for a total of 104,000 tonnes of U.S. soybeans and 88,000 tonnes of corn next week, traders said. State-owned Taiwan Sugar Corp may seek 18,000 tonnes of No.2 U.S. corn and 12,000 tonnes of No.2 U.S. soybeans for shipment from the U.S. Gulf from October 25 to November 10.

RICE TENDER - Sri Lanka will soon invite bids for 50,000 tonnes of rice for November/December delivery, officials of the state buying arm Cooperative Wholesale Establishment said. The new purchase will be for delivery in November and December and there will be no restrictions on rice origin.
MARKET TALK - The USDA authorized $1.075 billion in credit guarantees for sales of U.S. farm goods to Mexico under the Export Credit Guarantee Program (GSM-102) for fiscal 1997.
It also authorized $100 million to Turkey under GSM 102 for 1997. USDA offered $6 million to Estonia, $10 million to Slovakia and $25 million to Poland under GSM 102.

MARKET TALK Cont'd - Bulgaria lost a $25 million credit guarantee for the import of 120,000 tonnes of U.S. wheat after state-owned Bulbank refused to confirm the credit line on the grounds that the conditions were unfavourable, officials said on Tuesday. "The credit line for this year is lost. It is not renewable," U.S. embassy agriculture adviser William Huth told Reuters.

... One of Europe's largest soybean processors, Oelmuehle Hamburg AG, said on Tuesday it would begin importing and processing genetically modified soybeans from the U.S. this autumn, despite a protest campaign by environmentalist group Greenpeace. Oelmuehle said the genetically altered soybeans would constitute only one to two percent of its imports, but for practical reasons it could not separate them.
